history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this CSV row ("Kalyaneshwari Temple, Asansol", Asansol, West Bengal) is the same real temple as seq 1616 (id kalyaneshwari-temple-asansol) — the famous Kalyaneshwari Shakti shrine. CSV TOWN FLAG: the row says Asansol, but the temple does NOT stand in Asansol city; it is at Kalyaneshwari village on the Barakar River in PASCHIM BARDHAMAN district, WEST BENGAL, on the West Bengal-Jharkhand border, about 5 km downstream of the Maithon Dam and roughly 20 km from Asansol station. It is a circa-500-year-old centre of Shakti worship; legend says human sacrifices were offered here in the remote past. The present temple is not very old — Wikipedia says it was built by Sri Gurudin Prasad Pal, while other sources credit the Panchkot Raj (CONFLICT). The goddess is believed to be a living deity who fulfils the wishes of childless women. The name 'Maithon' is locally derived from 'Mai ka Sthan' (the Mother's place).

name: Kalyaneshwari Temple, Asansol
town_description: Kalyaneshwari is a small town near Asansol in Paschim Bardhaman district, West Bengal, right at the West Bengal-Jharkhand border on the Barakar River, about 5 km downstream of the Maithon Dam and just off the NH-19 bypass. It is best known for the centuries-old Maa Kalyaneshwari Shakti shrine, which draws pilgrims from both West Bengal and Jharkhand; the name 'Maithon' is locally derived from 'Mai ka Sthan' (the Mother's place).
